## Teaching at a glance

- **Instructor of record** for four courses at Michigan State University, from College
  Algebra to Multivariable Calculus, including an online course.
- **Teaching assistant and recitation leader** for six courses, including the
  graduate qualifying-exam course MTH 818 and, currently,
  [MTH 317H: Honors Linear Algebra](mth317h-fs26.qmd).
- **Lead Teaching Assistant** (Fall 2024, Spring 2025): observed classes and gave
  feedback to 8 teaching assistants and 16 undergraduate learning assistants.
- **Mentor**, MSU Summer Topology Program (Summer 2026): supervised two undergraduate
  projects in topology.

The full list of courses is on the [Teaching](../teaching.qmd) page.

## Certification in College Teaching {#cct}

I am completing the
[Certification in College Teaching](https://grad.msu.edu/professional-development/graduate-educator-advancement-and-teaching/certification-in-college-teaching) at Michigan State
University (expected Spring 2027). The program builds core competencies in college
teaching through coursework, workshops, and mentored practice.

### 1. Teaching college mathematics

- Coursework: **MTHE 879, Teaching College Mathematics**.
- Taught four courses as instructor of record, and wrote the recitation notes and
  worksheets for the proof-writing part of [MTH 317H](mth317h-fs26.qmd).

### 2. Creating effective learning environments

- Active-learning recitations built around collaboration, scaffolded tasks, and
  frequent low-stakes feedback (worksheets, quizzes, exit tickets).
- As Lead TA, observed classrooms and helped other instructors strengthen their
  learning environments.
- Tutor and supervisor at the Mathematics Learning Center for 6+ semesters.

### 3. Assessing student learning

- Proof-validation tasks and exit tickets give quick, actionable evidence of
  understanding.
- Separate student, answer-key, and instructor versions of materials support both
  practice and feedback.

### 4. Incorporating technology in teaching

- Taught MTH 124: Survey of Calculus fully online (Summer 2023).
- Course materials are typeset in LaTeX and published openly on this site.

### 5. Understanding the university context

- Completed the Certification in College Teaching Institute (May 2026). Topics included
  institutional contexts and missions, effective learning environments, assessment of
  student learning, and technology in teaching.
- Panelist at orientation for incoming Ph.D. students (Fall 2024).
- Department of Mathematics representative on the Council of Graduate Students
  (2025–2026).
